about: Guided question bank for the marks analysis call (Elements x Principles Matrix doc, Guide sequence, October 3, 2026). Element and principle keys come from app/core/design_fundamentals.json. Three steps: mark_meaning (seeing as), relationship (seeing that), principle_intent (what to bring out). The AI picks one of each step's question versions and fits it to the scene. It cannot add a step or a relationship type that is not listed here. Every step also takes a tap on the photo or the sketcher's own words (own_words). focal_suggestion and unseen ask about something no mark sits on.

actions.value_study: Dominant values: the photo simplified into a few flat value shapes, light to dark (OpenCV).
actions.grayscale: The Plan photo in black and white, until turned off in Guides, Value.
actions.grid: A square grid for the grid method.
actions.describe: Not an overlay. A short text field so the sketcher can answer in words. For naming what marks are.
actions.mark: Not an overlay. The sketcher answers by selecting marks on the Plan photo, in the guided questions of New Sketch only. The tap snaps to a point on the mark. The answer saves mark_ids and that point. For where and which answers.

own_words.about: The pencil row under every step's options. The sketcher types straight into it. A tap on empty space changes its placeholder to spot_placeholder.

focal_suggestion.about: Not chosen by the AI. Focal areas from the scene analysis are kept for comparing with the marks, never shown all at once. When no mark overlaps a focal area, the app asks this once for it, filling in $label (and $reason, if the wording uses it). While it shows, the app draws only that one area's outline, with a reticle. The first option adds the area as a mark along its outline (source 'prompted', adopted_region set). The others are only recorded.
focal_suggestion.question: Have you considered capturing the $label in your sketch?

mark_meaning.about: Seeing as. Once per object the guide asks about. The AI writes two readings, each tied to an element, and a short name for each (used as {A} or {B} in the next step).
questions: What do you see it as?

relationship.about: Seeing that. Once per pair of objects, or once for a lone object. The AI offers 2 or 3 types that fit, in the wording of 'option' (two objects) or 'option_one' (one object), fitted to the scene. {A} and {B} are filled with the sketcher's own names from mark_meaning. Only types with option_one can be offered for one object.
questions_two: How do {A} and {B} connect for you?
What do you see between {A} and {B}?
questions_one: What does {A} do in the scene?

gesture.looks_for: Figures or animals facing, reaching toward, or turning away from each other. A gaze or a lean is an implied line.
gesture.example: the two diners leaning toward each other across the table

echo.looks_for: Repeated shapes or colours in different subjects
echo.example: round lanterns echoing a round window

contrast.looks_for: Opposites side by side: old and new, big and small, rigid and organic
contrast.example: a glass tower beside a wooden shophouse
contrast.option: {A} and {B} are opposites side by side

scale.looks_for: A small subject set against a much larger one
scale.example: a lone cyclist under a flyover

framing.looks_for: One subject seen through or inside another
framing.example: a street seen through an archway

leading.looks_for: Lines that carry the eye from one subject to the other
leading.example: tram rails running toward a clock tower

temperature.looks_for: A warm area against a cold one. The warm one comes forward.
temperature.example: a red lantern against a blue-grey wall
temperature.option: The warm {A} stands out from the cool {B}
temperature.option_one: It is the warm spot in a cool scene

palette.looks_for: The scene held by one or two dominant colors
palette.example: a street all in ochre and terracotta
palette.option: {A} and {B} share the same few colors
palette.option_one: Its colors run through the whole scene

weight.looks_for: The weight on one side against the other: size, value, warm color, detail, isolation and distance from the center
weight.example: a large tree on the left against a small red boat on the right
weight.option: {A} on one side holds up {B} on the other

principle_intent.about: What to bring out. Asked after the relationship, with the options for the type the sketcher picked: that type's principle first, then one or two more from the same element's matrix row. Each option is a plain goal for this scene, never a principle name. A pick saves the principle as an intent (source intended). Up to max_principles across the plan.
questions: What do you want to bring out?

unseen.about: Asked only when no focal_suggestion is left. Gemini writes one question from a form_relationships entry that no mark sits on, and names the entry's element and principle. The options are fixed. The app shows a reticle on the first form.
unseen.question: Your marks leave out how these parts of the scene relate. Do you see it?

shape_balance.question: How do these shapes weigh against each other?

space_emphasis.question: What sets this subject apart from the rest?

line_movement.question: Where does this line lead the eye?

shape_pattern.question: Does this shape repeat elsewhere in the scene?

form_rhythm.question: These forms get smaller as they recede. How many will you draw?

options.label: A few, to suggest the row

line_proportion.question: What will you measure this line against?

shape_variety.question: Some of these shapes have hard edges and some are soft. Keep both?

line_unity.question: This line ties two parts of the scene together. How will you use it?

options.label: Keep it as a guide only
